name: Unke
prior: Direct ancestor in sound art: Felix Hess's 'electronic sound creatures' (first machine 1982, after hearing frog choruses in Australia in 1975) - small machines that call, respond to each other and 'fall silent as soon as they hear another sound'; fifty-creature installations that needed a silent hall (VS: earlabs.org/portfolio/felix-hess-frogs, isea-archives.siggraph.org/?p=39904, bldgblog.com 2008/04 quoting Toop's Ocean of Sound, deappel.nl 'Croaking and Chirping'). Science: Aihara et al. frog-chorus models with inhibitory/excitatory coupling and satellite males (VS: nal.ics.es.osaka-u.ac.jp i-aihara18rsos, arxiv.org/abs/2111.02640); tungara call timing = call when inhibition drops steeply (VS: datadryad.org 10.5061/dryad.3n5tb2rrz). Apps: Coqui Chorus (iOS) synthesises 11 frog species in real time with population, volume and distance - a soundscape, no documented responsive coupling, not pitch-playable (VS: apps.apple.com/app/id6760567046); Noisy Frog Sing-Along (children's app, recorded calls; VS: kirkusreviews.com). Hocket: Intellijel Shifty distributes a mono sequence over up to four voices ('hocketing') by rotation, no listening (VS: modulargrid.net intellijel-shifty, rubadub.co.uk). Frog-named timbre modules: Konstantine CROAK (prototype), MxRF Frog, ERD/TOAD (VS: modulargrid.net konstantine-croak-alpha-1, modulargrid.net other-unknown-mxrf-frog, lame.buanzo.org eurorack blog). In Myzel: Tropfen (random drips), Schwarm. Not found: a pitched, playable instrument whose voices listen to each other and call into the gaps; the playable form is new, the mechanism is Hess 1982.
costNotes: Per voice: PeriodicWave oscillator (cached, APP 3781) + lowpass + call gain + out = 4 nodes about 0.12-0.15 units, + an LFO/gain pair for the Schnarren above y 0.85 = 0.2 (R: webaudio.md section 4: ~0.03 per native node, biquad ~0.06-0.1); the idea's 0.25 is fair. L3 two frogs per voice L/R = 0.4. Scheduling: a main-thread unkTick with the app's lookahead (tick every 25 ms from the worker clock, horizon = currentTime + 0.12-0.35 s depending on jitter, APP 6033-6044) is exactly the rgTick pattern (APP 10674); each call is three gain events plus a frequency ramp, negligible. The shared register A.unk.calls is a list of (start, end, voice) including Puls hits; the scheduler must look up to one horizon ahead, so a Puls hit scheduled in the same tick must register before the fingers plan (order seqTick before unkTick, as the tick already does for seqTick). Simulation (sim/bio2_sim.py, call 0.2 s, shift behind the other's end + 40 ms, cap 2 own periods): three fingers produce a clean hocket - zero overlaps for y <= 0.7 - but the pond saturates: each voice is pinned at ~1.4 calls/s for y from 0.3 to 0.7 (own rate 1.7-4.5/s), so Hoehe stops changing the rate once three fingers are down; at y 0.85 (T = 0.153 s) the cap forces overlaps. One finger against a Puls lane of 8ths or 16ths at 120 bpm calls at 0.55/s instead of 1.73/s with waits up to 1.4 s - the lane nearly mutes the finger. Duty cycle of a held Unke: 25 % at y 0 (0.3 s of 1.2 s), 56 % at y 0.5.
soundHeld: A held finger is a creature, not a tone: at low Hoehe it calls 25 % of the time (a soft 'oop' every 1.2 s), so the first call must come within 150 ms at high velocity or the engine feels dead, and setF/Bebung are only audible during calls. The call itself - PeriodicWave 1/0.35/0.1 through a 2.5 f lowpass, 25 ms attack, 5 % downward bow - is close to Bombina's real soft 'unk' and close to a sine blip; the bow and the wet lowpass are all that separate it from Tropfen, so the Kehle and Bogen defaults must be strong. Three fingers: the hocket emerges by itself (sim: no overlaps up to y 0.7) and that is the genuinely new experience - a pond that answers. Weak spot: with three fingers the rate is pinned by the pond's capacity from y 0.3 to 0.7, so the Hoehe sweep does nothing in the middle; shrink the call length with y (0.35 -> 0.08 s) so capacity grows with excitement, and let Scheu < 1 permit overlaps with increasing probability so the top of the sweep merges into the Schnarren instead of jumping from a 6.5 Hz call train to an 18-30 Hz trill.
soundBurst: A Puls hit is a single call min(gate 0.22 s, call length) under burstEnv - a soft tuned 'oop' with a pitch bow, tempo-robust, registered so held fingers answer it. As a hit it is quiet and round (burstEnv attack >= 3 ms plus the call's own 25 ms attack = no transient), closer to a muted Tropfen than to Membran; its value is the dialogue it creates with held fingers, not the hit itself. Dense lanes (8ths/16ths) occupy the register and silence the fingers (sim: 0.55 of 1.73 calls/s, waits to 1.4 s) - weight lane hits as weaker inhibitors or exempt them when the lane is faster than 4 hits/s.
failureModes: Held note silent 75 % of the time at low Hoehe: feels dead without a fast first call and some audible presence (breath, throat resonance) between calls
Pond saturation: with 3+ fingers the call rate is pinned at ~1/(N x (call + gap)) for y 0.3-0.7, Hoehe loses its effect - call length must shrink with y and Scheu must allow overlaps
Dense Puls lanes mute held fingers (waits to 1.4 s, rate /3) - weaker inhibition for lane hits or a rate exemption
The single call is a soft sine-like blip; without the bow, wet lowpass and a touch of pulse structure it is Tropfen's poorer cousin
Hard jump from call train (6.5 Hz at y 0.85) to the 18-30 Hz Schnarren; needs a continuous rate/merge mapping
Calls off the Puls grid feel random against tight rhythmic presets; a 'Takt' option that quantises call slots to the grid is needed
Scheduling order: Puls hits must be registered before the fingers plan within the same tick, or fingers collide with hits already queued
verdict: Rare: Felix Hess's electronic sound creatures (1982 onward) already do exactly this - machines that call and fall silent when they hear another - but as installations; Coqui Chorus synthesises frog populations without listening, the Aihara models are science, Shifty hockets by rotation, so a pitched, playable listening chorus is not found and the playable form is new. Native and cheap (about 0.2 units, L3 0.4), scheduled from the app's existing 25-ms tick and lookahead like rgTick. The simulation confirms the hocket emerges (three fingers, zero overlaps up to y 0.7) and also exposes the limits: the pond saturates so Hoehe stops changing the rate between y 0.3 and 0.7 with three fingers, a 16th-note lane nearly mutes a held finger, and a low-Hoehe held note is silent 75 % of the time - fix with call length shrinking with Hoehe, Scheu < 1 permitting overlaps, weaker inhibition for lane hits and a guaranteed fast first call. The single call is a soft 'oop' next to a sine blip, so Puls hits are quiet and round; Unke is a strong world-building engine for held chords and lane dialogue, not a lead or a drum.
